question: Ethanol (alcohol) follows zero-order (saturation) kinetics at social drinking concentrations, meaning its rate of elimination is CONSTANT and independent of its plasma concentration.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Ethanol is the classic example of zero-order kinetics: alcohol dehydrogenase saturates at social drinking levels. Unlike first-order drugs (where a fixed fraction is eliminated per unit time), ethanol elimination is rate-limited at a constant amount per hour.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Alcohol dehydrogenase is saturated even at moderate ethanol concentrations. Therefore elimination proceeds at a fixed rate (~10–15 mL/hour) regardless of the plasma level — a clinically important zero-order drug.
